Naming only SLE omits the required SSc component of the overlap diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Captures only the SLE component of the overlap syndrome; misses the diffuse systemic sclerosis component

candidate_relations.reason: Skin thickening, salt-and-pepper lesions, capillaroscopy late signs, ILD, pulmonary hypertension, and skin biopsy findings strongly support diffuse SSc, but the anti-Sm positivity, low complement C3, lymphocytic ascites, and other features point to a concurrent SLE component that is not captured here.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Captures only the diffuse SSc component; misses the SLE component

candidate_relations.reason: Morning stiffness and hand arthritis with ulnar deviation could suggest RA, but the extensive skin, pulmonary, serological (anti-Sm, ANA patterns), and capillaroscopy findings are not explained by RA alone and point to a systemic sclerosis/SLE overlap.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: RA does not account for the dominant SSc and SLE features present

candidate_relations.reason: MCTD is a specific overlap syndrome defined by anti-U1-RNP antibody positivity with features of SLE, SSc, and myositis. The record shows anti-Sm (not anti-U1-RNP) and the combination of diffuse SSc and SLE features fits an SSc-SLE overlap rather than MCTD. Asserting MCTD conflicts with the required diagnostic specificity.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: MCTD is a distinct overlap entity (anti-U1-RNP-defined) and is not equivalent to SSc-SLE overlap syndrome

candidate_relations.reason: Ocular dryness and reduced Schirmer test results are present, but these are secondary sicca features commonly seen in SSc and SLE overlap. Sjögren's syndrome as a standalone diagnosis does not account for the dominant SSc and SLE findings.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Sicca symptoms are a manifestation/associated feature, not the primary diagnosis

case_quality_flags: Anti-U1-RNP not reported, which would be needed to formally exclude MCTD
Anti-Scl-70 and anti-centromere antibodies not reported, which would further characterize SSc subtype
Mitochondrial ANA pattern raises consideration of primary biliary cholangitis overlap, though ascitic fluid and clinical context favor SSc-SLE
